canonical_statement: Post-trial follow-up was designed to assess how the cardiorenal effects of empagliflozin evolved after discontinuation of randomized study drug.
EMPA-KIDNEY was a randomized comparison of empagliflozin 10 mg once daily versus matching placebo in patients with chronic kidney disease, with a median active-trial follow-up of 2.0 years.

canonical_statement: Post-trial follow-up was an optional substudy at 185 of 241 trial centers (77%) in seven of eight original countries; all surviving participants at participating centers were eligible.
No trial empagliflozin or placebo was administered during post-trial follow-up, while local practitioners could prescribe open-label SGLT2 inhibitors, including empagliflozin.

Post-trial reviews occurred every 6 months and collected vital status, kidney-replacement status, latest local creatinine, and current use of SGLT2 inhibitors, RAS inhibitors, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists.
More than 99% of reported end-stage kidney disease cases were confirmed locally, and deaths were centrally reviewed and categorized by blinded clinician adjudicators.
The prespecified primary post-trial assessment was time to kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death over the combined active- and post-trial periods.

concept.text: Kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death

outcome.definition: Kidney disease progression was sustained ≥40% eGFR reduction from randomization, end-stage kidney disease, sustained eGFR <10 mL/min/1.73 m², or kidney-failure death; sustained eGFR criteria required two consecutive measurements ≥30 days apart or were assumed for the final value before death, consent withdrawal, or completion.

canonical_statement: Kidney disease progression was defined using sustained eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, sustained eGFR below 10 mL/min/1.73 m², or death from kidney failure.

outcome.definition: Kidney disease progression was sustained ≥40% eGFR reduction from randomization, end-stage kidney disease, sustained eGFR <10 mL/min/1.73 m², or kidney-failure death; sustained eGFR criteria required two consecutive measurements ≥30 days apart or were assumed for the final value before death, consent withdrawal, or completion.

canonical_statement: Prespecified secondary outcomes included kidney disease progression alone and the composite of death from any cause or end-stage kidney disease, with end-stage kidney disease also analyzed separately.

concept.text: Death from any cause or end-stage kidney disease

canonical_statement: Time-to-event analyses used prespecified Cox proportional-hazards models adjusted for age, sex, prior diabetes, eGFR, UACR, and geographic region.
Kaplan–Meier estimates were used for time-to-event outcomes, and absolute benefit per 1000 assigned patients was calculated from between-group differences in Kaplan–Meier curves.
Because central samples were not collected post-trial, post-trial eGFR-based measurements were based on local laboratory values; active-trial primary events were carried forward in primary analyses.
A total of 6609 participants underwent randomization in the active trial.
Of the randomized participants, 4891 (74%) entered post-trial follow-up.
Post-trial participants were followed for a median 2.0 years (IQR 2.0–2.1).
At the end of post-trial follow-up, vital-status data were missing for 86 participants (1.8%) and 7 (0.1%) had withdrawn consent.
Among post-trial participants, mean age at randomization was 63±14 years and 1664 (34.0%) were women.
Among post-trial participants, 2784 of 4891 (56.9%) did not have diabetes.
Among post-trial participants, mean baseline eGFR was 36.9±14.1 mL/min/1.73 m².
Median baseline UACR in post-trial participants was 317 mg/g (IQR 44–1063), and 2393 (48.9%) had UACR ≤300 mg/g.
A nondiabetic cause of chronic kidney disease was recorded for 3487 post-trial participants (71.3%).
Randomized group blinding was maintained for 6578 of 6609 participants (99.5%) across the combined active- and post-trial periods.

During the active trial, SGLT2-inhibitor exposure averaged 90% in the empagliflozin group and 2% in the placebo group; during post-trial follow-up, open-label SGLT2 inhibitor use averaged 43% and 40%, respectively.
At approximately 12 months post-trial, open-label SGLT2 inhibitor use was 40.5% versus 37.4%; at approximately 24 months it was 45.4% versus 42.0% in prior empagliflozin versus prior placebo groups.
Average RAS-inhibitor use during post-trial follow-up declined over time but was 68% in both randomized groups.

Across the combined active- and post-trial periods, the primary outcome occurred in 865/3304 (26.2%) empagliflozin-assigned participants and 1001/3305 (30.3%) placebo-assigned participants (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.72–0.87).

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that empagliflozin continued to confer additional cardiorenal benefit for up to 12 months after discontinuation.
The authors interpreted the findings as suggesting that maximizing cardiorenal benefit from SGLT2 inhibition in chronic kidney disease requires long-term treatment.
The carryover effect was smaller than the on-treatment effect and appeared to last up to 12 months, with most additional post-trial benefit occurring in the first 6 months.

Reversal of the acute eGFR dip after SGLT2-inhibitor discontinuation could explain part of the post-trial benefit on eGFR-based progression components but does not explain the continuing end-stage kidney disease benefit.

Participants who did not initiate an open-label SGLT2 inhibitor post-trial had approximately twice the predicted kidney-failure risk of initiators, making observational post-trial comparisons by SGLT2 use confounded and unreliable.
Post-trial follow-up excluded patients from Japan, although active-trial treatment effects in Japan were reported as similar to other regions.
Post-trial kidney-function assessment relied on locally measured creatinine rather than central laboratory creatinine.
Hospitalization outcomes could not be assessed post-trial because hospitalization data were deliberately not collected during streamlined follow-up.

The trial was supported by Boehringer Ingelheim, with grant funding to the University of Oxford from Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly; additional CTSU support included the UK Medical Research Council and other public/charitable funders.
A data-sharing statement was provided with the full text of the article at NEJM.org.

The Supplementary Methods prespecified using local outpatient creatinine measurements preferentially over hospitalization measurements for post-trial eGFR ascertainment, because outpatient values were considered more representative of stable kidney function.

Supplementary absolute-benefit analyses calculated between-group differences from Kaplan–Meier curves and explained that in the absence of any off-treatment effect, absolute benefit should diminish after treatment cessation.

canonical_statement: Figure S2 presented sensitivity analyses of the primary composite using alternative handling of eGFR-based events, and the article reported results similar to the primary analysis.
Supplementary representativeness analyses documented that post-trial follow-up did not include Japan and enrolled no patients in Africa or Oceania.

Supplementary Table S2 showed that participants entering post-trial follow-up differed modestly from those not entering, including being less likely to be Asian and having slightly different kidney-risk characteristics.
The final post-trial follow-up Data Analysis Plan specified intention-to-treat analyses according to original randomized assignment over the combined active- and post-trial follow-up period.

canonical_statement: The post-trial protocol permitted open-label SGLT2-inhibitor use while preserving randomized treatment assignment as the primary analytic contrast.

The final Data Analysis Plan treated long-term eGFR slope as exploratory because discontinuation-related acute eGFR rebound and initiation of open-label SGLT2 inhibitors could distort slope interpretation.
